html:
A town founded in 1816 by the British officer Alexander Grant on St Mary's Island at the mouth of the Gambia River, named Bathurst. It was a base for patrols against the slave trade after Britain banned it in 1807.

Merchants, liberated Africans and Wolof traders settled there, and it became the seat of the Gambia colony and the port for the groundnut trade on the river. At independence in 1965 it was the capital, and in 1973 it was renamed Banjul. It is a small city on a crowded island, but most of the country's government and trade still runs through it. Nearby James Island was the older fort.
